To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
private firms with CEOs with experience outside the home province are more likely to engage in cross-province acquisitions than other firms.
private firms having CEO's experience outside of their home province are more likely to acquire firms in other provinces in the PRC.
the CEOs of private firms in China with experience in other provinces are more likely to conduct domestic acquisitions than CEOs of state-owned and foreign-invested enterprises.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel phenomenon, which has not been studied before, and provides important implications for both research and practice.
the drivers of cross-border acquisitions in China, and it is the first study to look at the drivers of crossprovince acquisitions of firms in an emerging economy.
domestic acquisitions in emerging markets, a phenomenon that has so far evaded scholars' interest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the drivers of cross province acquisitions are the CEOs with experience outside their home province, but this is only true for private firms.
the drivers of domestic acquisitions are different in different contexts.
the drivers of crossprovince acquisitions in China vary across ownership types.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CEO with prior experience is a critical driver for private firms to conduct domestic acquisitions.
private firms are the most likely drivers for cross-province acquisitions.
the drivers and moderators of cross-province acquisition decisions are different from that of cross-border acquisition decisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
domestic acquisitions in emerging economies are not just driven by the same forces that are driving international acquisitions, as is often assumed.
the resource-based view can be applied in explaining domestic acquisitions in emerging markets.
prior CEO experience and organizational slack do not have the same effects across different types of firms and locations of the acquiring firms.
